cards.text: Meet Manasseh, king of Judah, who takes the throne in Jerusalem at twelve years old and reigns FIFTY-FIVE years. Twelve years old! I've been around a whole lot longer than that, and I still can't run one little bakery without burning a batch.

cards.question: Manasseh does evil in the sight of the LORD. Whose abominations does he follow?

answers.text: The nations the LORD drove out
The kings who ruled in Egypt

cards.text: Here's what that evil looks like. His father Hezekiah had destroyed the high places, which is more cleaning up than my old junk drawer got in YEARS.

cards.question: Manasseh keeps the high places his father destroyed torn down.

cards.text: Manasseh rebuilds them, and he raises up altars for Baal too. That's like canceling every subscription you've got, and somebody signs you right back up for all of them PLUS a few new ones.

cards.question: Manasseh also makes an Asherah pole, just as King ___ of Israel had done.

cards.text: He worships and serves all the host of heaven, and I mean ALL of it. Now, about His own house, the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will put My Name."

cards.question: Where does Manasseh build altars to all the host of heaven?

answers.text: In the house of the LORD

cards.text: In both courtyards of the LORD's house. Then comes the darkest line in this whole passage: Manasseh sacrifices his own son in the fire.

cards.question: Manasseh practices sorcery and divination, and he consults ___ and spiritists.

cards.text: He does great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger. Then, and friend, I had to read this one twice, he takes the carved Asherah pole he made and sets it up in the temple itself.

And this isn't just any building, friend. This is the temple the LORD spoke about to King David and his son Solomon: "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever."

cards.question: God also promised He'd never again make Israel wander from the land He gave their fathers. What was the condition?

answers.text: They had to do all He commanded
They had to defeat their enemies
They had to build Him more altars

cards.question: The people of Judah refuse to follow Manasseh into evil.
Manasseh leads the people astray. How does their evil compare to the nations the LORD destroyed before Israel?

cards.text: The LORD doesn't stay quiet. He speaks through His servants the prophets: Manasseh has acted more wickedly than the Amorites who came before him, and with his idols he has caused Judah to sin.

cards.question: The LORD says He is bringing peace and security to Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.text: He's bringing calamity, so big the news will reverberate in the ears of all who hear it. Not one little group chat ping, friend, but every phone in town buzzing at the SAME time.

God says He'll stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line used against Samaria and the plumb line used against the house of Ahab. Then He gives a picture I know from my own kitchen: He'll wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes out a bowl.

cards.question: God says He'll wipe out Jerusalem like a bowl. After the wiping, what happens to the bowl?
What does God say He will do with the remnant of His inheritance?

cards.text: They'll become plunder and spoil to all their enemies. And friend, God doesn't leave anybody guessing why.

cards.question: God says they have provoked Him to anger from the day their fathers came out of ___ until this day.

cards.text: On top of all that, Manasseh sheds so much innocent blood that he fills Jerusalem from end to end. And believe it or not, there's more, all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

cards.question: After his long reign, Manasseh rests with his fathers. Where is he buried?

cards.text: The garden of Uzza, to be exact, and his son Amon takes the throne at twenty-two and reigns in Jerusalem TWO years. I've forgotten cookie dough in the back of the fridge longer than that.

cards.question: Amon turns away from his father's evil and does what is right in the sight of the LORD.
Amon walks in all the ways of his father, and he serves and worships the ___ his father had served.

cards.text: He abandons the LORD, the God of his fathers, and doesn't walk in the way of the LORD. Then, oh NO, a plot forms against the king.

cards.question: Who conspires against King Amon and kills him in his palace?
The people of the land side with the servants who killed King Amon.

cards.text: Talk about a plan that backfires: the people of the land kill all those who conspired against Amon and make his son Josiah king in his place. Amon is buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and young Josiah takes the throne.

findings.problem: The setup opens with "Here's what that evil looks like" and then says Hezekiah had destroyed the high places. That framing rules out "True" on card 4 (Manasseh keeping them torn down) before the baker reasons about anything.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks where Manasseh builds altars to all the host of heaven. That is only stated in 2 Kings 21:5. Verse 4 says he built altars in the LORD's house but doesn't say they were to the host of heaven, yet the card cites 2 Kings 21:4-5.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Card 4 stops partway through the line "as one wipes out a bowl". This card then asks what happens to the bowl next, which is the rest of that line: "wiping it and turning it upside down". The baker is guessing wording. "It's set on the table" is just as reasonable a guess as the right answer.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card has more than two beats: the people kill the conspirators, they make Josiah king, Amon is buried, and Josiah takes the throne. It also tells Josiah becoming king twice.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "Young Josiah" adds a fact that isn't in 2 Kings 21. Josiah's age is given in 2 Kings 22:1, but the card gives no reference for it and cites only 2 Kings 21:24-26.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "In his palace garden" is a wrong answer on stop 1 card 8 (where Manasseh builds altars) and the right answer here (where he is buried). It is false as a wrong answer on card 8, but a baker who remembers seeing it marked wrong may be steered away from it here.
findings.question: Can a phrase used as a wrong answer on one card be the right answer on a later card in the same walkthrough, or should one of them be reworded or replaced?
